messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: sev1 - routing-service: smart-routing fallback triggered for EU customer traffic to us-west-2 (possible data residency violation). Pager: oncall-maya. Links: https://alerts.redwood.internal/1867000000

maya: taking this. more context? seeing spike in fallback rate?

jordan: I see the same in metrics: smart-route fallback ratio for customer_scope=eu-telehealth jumped from 0.2% -> 18% at 06:03 UTC. Logs show `policy_evaluation=allow_fallback=true` for requests with residency=eu.

sam: that's wrong — residency should block region change for that customer. Config commit 9f3b4a applied ~06:02 looks related to fallback thresholds. pinging alex to confirm recent rollout.

alex: I rolled the routing policy patch to lower latency fallbacks earlier today. It included a change to default fallback behavior `allow_fallback: true` for certain tiers. I did not intend to override residency. reverting now.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) disable inter-region fallback globally for residency-constrained customers 2) roll back commit 9f3b4a 3) run scrub to identify affected requests and notify privacy-ops. Who can run the rollback now?

jordan: I can run rollback and flip the policy flag. Command:```cli
# revoke cross-region fallback for residency-protected routes
rictl routing set --selector "labels.residency=eu" --set "fallback.policy=deny"
```

sam: I'll apply a quick ACL at the edge to block egress to us-west-2 for eu-residency routes while rollback completes:```bash
curl -X POST $EDGE_API/acl -d '{"rule":"block","dest":"us-west-2","selector":"residency=eu"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

lina: customer-facing: several eu customers (IDs: cust-112, cust-118, cust-220) reported anomalous logs where their data appeared in us-west-2. We need a short impact blurb for SOC/comms.

privacy-ops: please capture sample request ids and timestamps. recommend rotating any ephemeral keys used during window and prepare notification if PHI exposed.

maya: jordan, confirm when rollback applied and what window of impacted requests we'll need to redact/notify.

jordan: rollback done at 06:08 UTC. `fallback.policy` set to `deny` for matching routes. Edge ACL applied at 06:06 UTC by sam. Current fallback rate back to baseline.

jordan: affected window: 06:02:10 - 06:08:00 UTC. I pulled logs and found ~2.1k requests that matched residency=eu but routed to us-west-2. sample ids: req_8a3f, req_9b2d, req_a77c. Saved to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/1867000000/requests.csv

privacy-ops: thanks. starting impact assessment. Are we sure model variant was compatible (same weights) or did a model variant mismatch happen too?

sam: quick look: model variants were same family but different region replicas (quantization/regional caches differ) — risk level: medium for data residency; low for model correctness.

alex: timeline note: the rollout unintentionally left `residency_override` unset for customers with label `compliance=high`. The intent was to default to deny, but config merge error flipped it. I'll open an immediate revert PR and add an automated test.

maya: action items: - Notify SOC + legal with impact window and sample ids (privacy-ops) - Customer success: notify affected customers with proposed remediation & offer audit (lina) - Postmortem owner: alex - Add gating test for residency flags in CI (alex/jordan) - Follow-up: confirm no persisted copies left in us-west-2 (sam)

lina: drafting customer message now. short note, no promise yet on root cause, will say we detected and blocked unintended routing, investigating, will follow up within 24h.

privacy-ops: initial triage: no evidence of long-term storage in us-west-2 S3 buckets; ephemeral caches may have contained KV snippets. We'll do a scan and produce a data exposure assessment by EOD.

jordan: putting a temporary alert rule stricter: `alert if fallback_rate>1% for residency=eu` and add runbooks to auto-disable fallback.

sam: I revoked any temporary credentials used by routing service for cross-region caching at 06:12 UTC.

maya: handing off to daytime oncall jordan for next steps and RCA. I'm incident lead for now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

jordan: taking post-incident. I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem invite and link the rollback PR and metrics in the incident doc. Postmortem owner: alex (config/rollout).

alex: created PR #4523 to revert 9f3b4a and added CI test. Also adding a pre-deploy check to verify `residency_override` defaults.

privacy-ops: final note: if the scan finds any PHI in ephemeral caches we'll follow our disclosure playbook. keep customer comms aligned with legal.

maya: closing pager. last status: fallback disabled, edge ACL in place, rollback merged to hotfix branch. Will reopen if anything reappears.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged: sev1 -> transitioned to post-incident review. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1867000000/postmortem
